title: Nuclear plant accident or fallout
summary: Get inside, stay inside, stay tuned. Take potassium iodide only if officials say so.

items.text: Get alerts from several sources: the FEMA app, local community alerts and a battery-powered or hand-crank radio.
Keep an emergency kit with a spare change of clothes per person, a trash bag for contaminated clothing, and sealed food, water and medicine.
Make a family plan: a meeting place, an out-of-state contact, backup places to stay, and the shelter plans at school, work and care facilities.
Know your evacuation route and your nearest Evacuation Assembly Center.
items.note: Virginia says to plan to be away from home at least three days if ordered to evacuate.

items.text: After any blast, get into the nearest sturdy building fast. You have 10 minutes or more before fallout arrives.
items.note: Brick or concrete buildings, basements, underground parking garages and subways are best.

items.text: Stay in the most protective spot, such as a basement or the center of a large building, for **at least 24 hours**.
items.note: Leave sooner only for an immediate hazard like fire or collapse, or if authorities say it is safe.

items.text: Turn off fans, air conditioning and forced-air heating. Close windows, doors and fireplace dampers.
Bring pets and service animals inside.
Keep listening to your local Emergency Alert System radio or TV station.
Take potassium iodide (KI) **only** if emergency officials or a healthcare provider tell you to.
items.note: KI protects only the thyroid. Use FDA-approved KI only, as directed. Do not leave shelter to look for it.

items.text: If ordered to evacuate: go to your nearest Evacuation Assembly Center.
items.note: Pets and service animals are allowed there.

items.text: Remove your outer layer of clothing, which can remove up to 90% of radioactive material.
items.note: Move slowly and keep your hands away from your eyes, nose and mouth. Bag the clothes.

items.text: Shower or wash with soap and water. If you cannot, wipe exposed skin and hair with a wet cloth.
items.note: Hand sanitizer does not protect against radioactive material.

items.text: Brush your pet's coat, then wash the pet with soap and water if available.
Food and water from inside a building are safe. Wipe sealed containers from outside with a damp cloth first.
items.note: Do not eat garden produce or uncovered outdoor food or drink until authorities say it is safe.

items.text: If you evacuated, do not return until local authorities say it is safe.
If you are sick or injured, follow instructions on where to get medical care. At a shelter, tell staff right away.
